title: Sport
subtitle: hang-gliding, a tennis racket, get knocked out
summary: Name less common sports and their equipment, describe athletics events, and talk about winning, losing and records.

lesson.heading: Some sports you may not know the names of
rows: you run off a hill under a large wing and glide through the air
you roll a heavy ball along a lane at ten pins; the ball curves, so you aim away from the centre
two people fight with thin swords
a horse has to get over a series of jumps without knocking the posts off
you stand on a board with a sail; it is all a matter of balance
you come down a mountain standing sideways on one wide board
you swim under water with a tank of air on your back
you hit coloured balls into pockets on a table; the colours are worth different points
noisy, fast and dangerous, but exciting to watch
you shoot arrows at a target
you throw small pointed darts at a board; you need a good eye and concentration

lesson.heading: Equipment - what you hold in your hand
Athletics
lesson.text: The track and field events are the **discus (throw)**, the **javelin**, the **high jump**, the **long jump**, the **pole vault** and **gymnastics**. In the discus you throw a heavy disc a long way; in the javelin you throw a long pole with a sharp point.

examples.note: = fast over short distances, e.g. 100 metres

examples.text: He's doing a **marathon** next month - 42 kilometres, or 26 miles.
The **long jump** covers a long distance in one jump; the **high jump** goes over a bar.

lesson.heading: Competition in sport
lesson.text: You **set** a record when you make a new best time; you **hold** the record while nobody has beaten it. If you **qualify** you reach the necessary standard; if you are **knocked out** in a **round**, you lose at that stage and leave the competition.

examples.text: She **set** a new Olympic record last year.
He **holds** the record for the 100 metres breaststroke.
England **qualified** for the World Cup but got **knocked out** in the third **round**.
Our team **made it to** the semi-final but then we were beaten.
Most sports are very **competitive** these days.
examples.note: = they involve a strong desire to win

lesson.heading: Trophies, referees and spectators
lesson.text: A **trophy** is the cup or other object that shows you have won. The **referee** controls the match; the **spectators** are the people present to watch it, and the team's **fans** support it everywhere.

examples.text: She felt proud as she held the **trophy** in her hands.
Thousands of **spectators** protested loudly at the decision of the **referee**.
Players who disagree with the **referee** set a bad example to their **fans**.

lesson.heading: People who do particular sports
rows: tennis player, squash player, basketball player
a word you must learn separately
lesson.note: Say archer, not ~~archerer~~; tennis player, not ~~tenniser~~; golfer, not ~~golfist~~.

lesson.text: In British English the noun *sport* goes into the plural in front of another noun: *sports equipment*, *sports facilities*, *sports club* - not ~~sport equipment~~.

exercises.prompt: Which sport is each person talking about?

pairs.left: 'Provided it's not too windy at the top of the hill, there's no problem.'
'It is incredibly noisy, fast and dangerous, but it's exciting to watch.'
'The horse has to get over the jumps without knocking the posts off.'
'It's all a matter of balance. Sometimes you can't help falling in the water.'
'The different ball colours are worth different numbers of points.'
'It's a fantastic feeling when the snow flies up into the air around you.'

exercises.prompt: Name the piece of equipment you hold for each sport.
She's won a lot of ___ in the last five years and has them all in a glass cabinet at her house.
exercises.explanation: A trophy is the cup or other object you get for winning.

exercises.prompt: He's doing a ___ next week - running 42 kilometres! That's 26 miles!
exercises.explanation: A marathon is a 42-kilometre race for long-distance runners.

exercises.prompt: Who ___ the world record for the 1,000 metres these days? Is it a Russian?
exercises.explanation: You set a record once; you hold it until somebody beats it.

exercises.prompt: His national team failed to ___ for the World Cup, so he's supporting Brazil instead.
exercises.explanation: Qualify = reach the standard needed to enter the competition.

exercises.prompt: My team got knocked out in the second ___ of the competition. We were disappointed it happened so early.
exercises.explanation: A competition is played in rounds; if you are knocked out you leave it.

exercises.prompt: All Olympic sports are highly ___; everyone has one ambition - to win gold.
exercises.explanation: Competitive is the adjective: it describes a strong desire to win.

exercises.prompt: In which athletics event do you throw a heavy disc a long way?
exercises.explanation: The discus (throw). In the javelin you throw a pole with a sharp point.

exercises.prompt: How do we name the person who does each sport?

exercises.statement: She was a champion gymnastic when she was a teenager.
exercises.explanation: She was a champion gymnast when she was a teenager. Gymnastics is the sport; a gymnast is the person.

exercises.statement: My brother is an expert canoeist. He's won medals.
exercises.explanation: Correct. The person who goes canoeing is a canoeist.

exercises.statement: Is there a shop near here that sells sport equipment? I need a fishing rod.
exercises.explanation: Is there a shop near here that sells sports equipment? In British English sport takes -s before another noun.
